o: Negative numbers act as frozen anchors: their positions never change. We collect the values sitting at non-negative positions, rotate that value list left by k cyclically, then write the rotated values back into those same positions in order. In [1,-2,3,-4] the movable values are [1,3]; rotating left by 3 is the same as rotating by 3 mod 2 = 1, giving [3,1]; writing back yields [3,-2,1,-4]. With n up to 1e5 and k up to 1e5, reducing k modulo the count of non-negative elements keeps everything linear.
k: Only the relative order of non-negative values rotates; negative slots are fixed scaffolding.
k should be reduced modulo m (number of non-negative elements) to avoid wasted work.
Extraction, rotation, and write-back are three independent linear passes.

a.i: Record the indices holding non-negative values and gather those values. Rotating a list left by k is just concatenating its suffix from index k mod m with its prefix. Writing rotated values back into the recorded indices restores negatives untouched.
s: Collect idx = indices with nums[i] >= 0 and vals = corresponding values.
Set k = k mod len(vals) (skip if vals is empty).
Assign vals[p] back to nums[idx[p]] for each p.
a.t: O(n) — three linear passes over indices/values.
a.sp: O(n) — the index and value buffers.

a.i: Push non-negative values onto a deque and use its built-in cyclic rotation (rotate(-k) in Python, poll/offer in Java). This delegates the modular arithmetic to the library and reads cleanly, at identical asymptotic cost.
s: Collect non-negative values into a deque and their indices into a list.
Rotate the deque left by k mod m.
Pop values from the deque front and write them into the recorded indices.
a.t: O(n + k mod m) — collection pass plus the rotation shifts.

w: Use Approach 1 as the default — slice rotation is simplest and fastest. Watch for: an array with zero non-negative elements (skip everything), k larger than m (must mod), and mutating input vs. returning a copy depending on expectations. A follow-up might demand O(1) extra space via reversal tricks applied only to the extracted subsequence.
